events.title: First Continental Congress Convenes
events.description: Delegates from twelve of the thirteen American colonies met at Carpenters' Hall in Philadelphia to coordinate a response to the Coercive Acts imposed by Britain after the Boston Tea Party.
events.significance: The Congress marked the first major step toward colonial unity and laid the groundwork for the American Revolution and the eventual formation of the United States.

events.title: Peter the Great Imposes a Beard Tax
events.description: Tsar Peter I of Russia introduced a tax on beards to encourage Russian nobles and merchants to adopt Western European grooming styles.
events.significance: The tax symbolized Peter's broader campaign to modernize and Westernize Russia, reshaping Russian culture and society.

events.title: Munich Olympics Massacre
events.description: Eight members of the Palestinian group Black September took Israeli athletes and coaches hostage at the Munich Summer Olympics. A failed rescue attempt resulted in the deaths of eleven Israeli team members and a West German police officer.
events.significance: The attack shocked the world, transformed security at international sporting events, and influenced counterterrorism policy and the creation of specialized units worldwide.

events.title: Death of Mother Teresa
events.description: Mother Teresa, the Albanian-Indian Catholic nun who founded the Missionaries of Charity, died in Calcutta (Kolkata), India, at age 87.
events.significance: Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her work with the poor and dying, she became a global symbol of charity and was canonized as a saint in 2016.

events.title: Voyager 1 Launched
events.description: NASA launched the Voyager 1 space probe from Cape Canaveral, Florida, to study Jupiter, Saturn, and beyond.
events.significance: Voyager 1 became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space in 2012 and remains the most distant spacecraft from Earth.
